caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:alm-1
attempts.paper_title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement
attempts.entry_title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement (Li et al. 2015)
attempts.summary: The paper's electrophysiology findings largely held up in this data, while its behavioural and imaging findings could not be tested because those recordings are not in the dataset. ALM selectivity matched: 912 of 1,245 pyramidal neurons were selective, contra- and ipsi-preferring neurons were equally common, and activity on error trials followed the licking direction. Pyramidal tract neurons, unlike intratelencephalic neurons, were mostly contra-preferring when only selective neurons were counted, and their late contralateral selectivity matched in size but not in onset or in its comparison with all selective neurons. The licking effects of photoinhibiting ALM and of photoactivating pyramidal tract neurons are among the missing data. Minor claims on spike widths, fast-spiking neurons and antidromic jitter held in part.
attempts.description: Tests the electrophysiology findings of Li, Chen, Guo, Gerfen and Svoboda (2015) on CRCNS data set alm-1, which holds 1,408 units recorded in left ALM of 19 mice over 99 sessions of a delayed tactile discrimination task, with PT and IT neurons identified by antidromic tagging. It tests trial-type selectivity and its time course, response categories, error trials, contra and ipsi preference, fast-spiking neurons, antidromic latencies, and the contralateral selectivity of PT neurons. The photoinhibition and photoactivation behaviour, the imaging and the anatomy are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2015) from CRCNS alm-1

outcomes.notes: The photoinhibition behaviour (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP and PV-ires-Cre x ReaChR mice) is not in the data set, which holds only the 19 electrophysiology mice; its trials carry axonal tagging stimulation, not ALM photoinhibition. The data description names no other deposit, and none was found on CRCNS.
Same data as fig1d-photoinhibition-ipsilateral-bias, not in the data set.

Control trials, mean over sessions (reading a), 76.84% correct and 10.88% lick early trials; over mice 76.37% and 14.06%; pooled 77.28% and 12.59%. With all trials except the NaN-type test trials, 76.09% to 76.59% correct. Every reading puts the per cent correct within 78.4 +/- 7.84; the lick early fraction is below 14.3% under every reading but the mean over mice with all trials but NaN-type (14.69%). Per mouse 60.4% to 87.0% correct.
deviations: Measured on the 19 electrophysiology mice in the data set; the paper's figure is over 42 mice, and the behaviour-only mice are not deposited.
No-lick trials are left out of the denominator, as the data set's Demo_get_performance.m does; the Methods say only that lick early trials are excluded.

outcomes.notes: 1,408 units, 19 mice, 99 sessions. The trough-to-peak widths of the deposited mean waveforms (the criterion's measure) give 1,245 units above 0.45 ms, 158 below 0.35 ms and 5 in between, so the FS and intermediate counts are outside tolerance; 34 of the 39 units without a label have widths below 0.35 ms. A spline-interpolated variant gives 1,241, 158 and 9. The data set's cellType labels give exactly 1,245 pyramidal, 124 FS and 39 unlabelled units. The waveform arrays hold 29 samples per spike and one row per spike in every unit, with the trough at sample 15. The labels split the deposited widths cleanly - FS 0.154 to 0.256 ms, unlabelled 0.307 (34) or 0.410 ms (5), pyramidal 0.461 to 0.666 ms - so the labels put the FS boundary between 5 and 6 samples, not at 0.35 ms. The paper's classification is in the labels but its stated thresholds do not give it from the deposited waveforms.
deviations: Waveforms are the deposited 29-sample snippets at 19531.25 Hz, so widths come in steps of 0.0512 ms; the paper does not say whether its widths were interpolated.

outcomes.notes: With lick early trials dropped and a 1.3 s response epoch, 912 of 1,245 pyramidal neurons (73.25%) are selective, exactly the paper's count. The other readings give 910 to 950; Welch's test 903 to 947; the t-test on spike counts 912 under the main readings and 910 to 944 under the others. All within tolerance. Per mouse 0.417 to 0.852.
deviations: The t-test is on spike rates (count over each trial's epoch length), as the data set's analysis_compile_all_data.m runs it (lines 217 to 221 and 300, printed in the notebook); the Methods say spike counts, which differ where an epoch is not 1.3 s (3,707 trials), and the test on counts is shown as a variant.

Trials with axonal photostimulation (types 1 to 5 and NaN) and trials with GoodTrials 0 are left out, and each unit's trials are limited to the span from its first to its last trial with a spike, as the data set's analysis_compile_all_data.m does; the paper does not state either.

outcomes.notes: 219 preparatory only, 389 with both and 304 peri-movement only, exactly the figure's reading (b), under the main readings; the text's reading (a), 389 peri-movement only and 304 both, does not match under any reading of the response epoch or lick early trials. Measured values are given in the order of the expected values (preparatory only, peri-movement only, both).
deviations: The text and Fig. 2d disagree on which of 389 and 304 is the peri-movement-only count; the data match the figure (recorded as a paper inconsistency).

outcomes.notes: Significant neurons in 200 ms windows, 60 before sample onset (shuffled labels median 54), 246 at the end of the sample, 298 and 379 at the start and end of the delay, peak 554 at 0.19 s after the cue. Population selectivity of 880 selective neurons with at least 11 trials of each type, 0.005, 1.19, 1.46 and 2.28 spikes/s at those times, peak 3.38 at 0.20 s. All three conditions hold for both measures under both readings.
deviations: The 10 trials that set each neuron's preference are drawn at random with a fixed seed; the preference uses spike counts from sample onset to the end of the response epoch, as the data set's compile script does. Neurons need 11 trials of each type for the split (848 with more than 15, as the script requires, give the same).

outcomes.notes: Mean population response correlation with the cue-time vector over the sample epoch and the first 0.5 s of the delay is -0.168 (reading a) and -0.159 (reading b); -0.041 and -0.084 with division by the s.d. Population selectivity stays above 0 from the end of the sample epoch through the delay (minimum 1.19 spikes/s).
deviations: The 0.5 bound is the claims file's assumption read from Fig. 2c; the paper gives no threshold.

outcomes.notes: Pearson's r between correct and error selectivity is negative in every epoch under both readings and the script's selection; sample -0.085 to -0.123 (P 0.006 to 0.017), delay -0.43 to -0.48, response -0.44 to -0.50 (printed P < 0.0001). The fraction of neurons switching sign is 0.507 to 0.652, above one half in all epochs; in the sample epoch the effect is weak. Under the four readings of the shared methods the sample r is -0.082 to -0.097 (P 0.004 to 0.018) and the switched fractions 0.502 to 0.627. 69 of 912 selective neurons have no error trials of one type.

427 contra-preferring and 485 ipsi-preferring selective pyramidal neurons by total counts (reading a), the Fig. 2c counts exactly; bootstrap P for more contra-preferring neurons 0.97. With the 10-trial split 436 and 444 (P = 0.60). The four readings of the shared methods give 427 to 458 contra and 479 to 492 ipsi (P 0.86 to 0.97). A binomial test against 0.5 gives p = 0.059.

Mean lick right minus lick left rate, 0.090 spikes/s for selective pyramidal neurons (P = 0.44), 0.061 for all pyramidal (P = 0.48), 0.071 for all units (P = 0.39); not significant under any reading; the four readings of the shared methods give P 0.18 to 0.62. The paper reports P = 0.13.

FS baseline rates are higher under both readings (mean 9.03 against 3.97 spikes/s, median 6.40 against 2.37). FS are not less selective under either criterion reading - 79.8% selective against 73.3%, mean absolute rate difference 2.29 against 1.53 spikes/s. Only the rate difference relative to the mean rate, a variant the criterion does not name, makes FS less selective (median 0.21 against 0.33). The four readings of the shared methods give the same (FS 79.8% to 84.7% selective against 73.1% to 76.3%). The baseline half holds, the selectivity half does not, so the claim holds in part.

The labels give 45 PT neurons (8 mice) and 27 IT neurons (7 mice), the paper's counts. The activated neurons that failed the collision test (22 and 106) and the 7 untestable ones carry no label, so those counts cannot be reported, and no measured list is given.

First pulses, spikes within +/-1 ms of each neuron's modal latency. PT 2.672 ms and 0.126 ms jitter (45 neurons), within tolerance; IT 4.98 ms (21 neurons with type 2 trials) or 4.56 ms (27 neurons, types 2 to 5), within tolerance and longer than PT. IT jitter 0.310 ms (0.265 with types 2 to 5) and the tagged mean 0.184 ms (0.178) are outside tolerance. The order and the PT values hold, the IT jitter and the tagged mean do not; the four activated-neuron values cannot be computed, as those neurons are not labelled, so no measured list is given. Readings without a window agree with +/-1 ms - a per-neuron fit of a Gaussian peak plus a uniform background gives IT jitter 0.341 ms and a tagged mean of 0.185 ms, the same fit with a broad component added 0.282 and 0.166 ms, and the +/-1 ms window without the four IT neurons with broad humps 0.289 and 0.170 ms. A robust s.d. (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation within +/-1 ms) gives 0.289 and 0.166 ms. Only the +/-0.5 ms window gives values within tolerance (IT 0.198 ms, 0.177 with types 2 to 5; tagged mean 0.140 ms). PT jitter is 0.112 to 0.126 ms under every reading. This claim and reaction-time each turn on a detection rule the paper does not give, but they differ. Here the PT values, the latencies and their order hold under every window, and five of the six jitter readings agree on the IT jitter. For reaction-time the single value falls inside or outside tolerance with the rule, and the data give no reason to prefer any rule.
deviations: The paper does not say how antidromic spikes are told from spontaneous ones. Assumed - the first spike within 10 ms of a pulse, kept when within +/-1 ms of the neuron's modal latency (0.2 ms bins). Between 0.5 and 1 ms from the mode the IT neurons have 783 spikes where the spontaneous background (latencies more than 2 ms from the mode) predicts 69.7. This shows the spikes are locked to the pulse, not that they are antidromic - several IT neurons show humps several ms wide, and the four broadest hold 316 of the 783 spikes. The window rests instead on the readings that need none (fits of a narrow peak plus background, with and without a broad component), which give IT jitter near the +/-1 ms value. The +/-0.5 ms window, adopted before verification, is shown as a variant.
Pulse onsets are read from the AOM input trace at 10 kHz, so they are quantised to 0.1 ms, and any delay between the AOM input and the light is not known.
IT tagging trials are type 2; types 3 to 5, undocumented, are included as a variant.

outcomes.notes: Mean IT jitter is lower for the second pulse in all four variants (type 2 trials, +/-0.5 ms, 0.156 against 0.204 ms; types 2 to 5, +/-1 ms, 0.232 against 0.280 ms), and 65% to 87% of IT neurons decrease (Wilcoxon p 0.004 to 0.098). 4 to 8 IT neurons with fewer than three responses to a pulse are left out.
deviations: Antidromic spikes are selected as in antidromic-latency-jitter.

outcomes.notes: Selective PT neurons 7 preparatory only, 16 both, 15 peri-movement only of 38 (0.184, 0.421, 0.395; Fig. 3e about 0.18, 0.43, 0.40); selective IT neurons 5, 13, 5 of 23 (0.217, 0.565, 0.217; Fig. 3i about 0.22, 0.56, 0.22). Both populations hold both kinds under every reading.

Selective neurons (reading b), lick early dropped, 1.3 s response epoch; PT 24 of 38 contra-preferring (0.632, P = 0.033), IT 10 of 23 (0.435, P = 0.74, the paper's value). With lick early kept PT P = 0.017 (1.3 s) and 0.037 (1.5 s); with a 1.5 s response epoch and lick early dropped P = 0.068. All tagged neurons (reading a) give PT 27 of 45 (0.600, P = 0.089) and IT P = 0.58, so the PT part does not hold under reading a (P 0.089 to 0.23 over the four readings of the shared methods). Selective neurons with more than 15 correct trials of each type, a variant outside the criterion's readings, give PT 19 of 32 (0.594, P = 0.11; 0.054 to 0.20 over the four readings), so the PT part does not hold under that filter either. The data set's IT_PT script applies that filter to the curve of all selective pyramidal neurons (line 25) and takes the PT and IT fractions from the selective neurons without it (lines 170 and 195).

Over the 570 ms before the cue, PT modulation is 34.4% of the window rate (P = 0.027), the paper's value, and IT -16.4% (P = 0.11), but all task-selective neurons give 9.2% with P = 0.024, significant where the paper has P = 0.13. Over the window to the end of the response epoch all task-selective neurons are not significant (P = 0.96) but neither is PT (20.6%, P = 0.068). No combination of readings gives the paper's pattern of significance. The PT contra-selectivity stays significant from 310 ms before the cue (reading a; first significant 2,480 ms before, reading b), against 570 ms. Under the four readings of the shared methods (lick early trials dropped or kept, response epoch 1.3 or 1.5 s) all task-selective neurons give P = 0.022 to 0.024 in the pre-cue window, the onset is 190 to 310 ms (a) or 2,470 to 2,490 ms (b), and none of the 32 combinations has the paper's pattern. The PT and IT part of the claim holds in the pre-cue window; the comparison with all selective neurons and the onset do not.

The paper does not say how the first mouth movement is found in the photodiode trace, and the result crosses the tolerance within the range of plausible rules. Noise rule (first sample from which the trace stays for 5 ms further from its pre-cue median than k times the noise and at least a floor), correct trials of type 0, mean over 19 mice of per-mouse means - 65.0 ms (s.d. 21.1) at k = 3 and 2 mV, within 61.1 +/- 10.5; 71.7 ms at k = 3 and 5 mV, just outside; 77.7 to 103.7 ms at k = 5 and 10. On all responses k = 3 gives 65.0 and 71.3 ms, both within. The peak rule (a fraction of each trial's largest excursion) gives 81.7 to 176.8 ms (s.d. 57 to 65 ms). Neither threshold is better founded - in the 0.1 s before the cue the noise rule fires in 11.6% to 16.0% of correct trials at k = 3 and 6.5% to 8.2% at k = 5. The spread across mice is 21 to 36 ms under the noise rule, two to three times the paper's 10.5 ms. Per-session means (k = 5, 5 mV) range from 34 to 212 ms, and in some sessions the trace is a two-level signal or carries cue-locked deflections (example traces in the notebook).
deviations: The paper does not say how the first movement is found in the photodiode trace, and the trace's baseline (0.07 to 4.83 V), scale and sign differ between sessions. Two rules are run, the noise rule (k = 3, 5, 10; floor 2 or 5 mV; 5 ms hold) and the peak rule (5% to 50% of the trial's peak excursion). No choice among them has a basis in the paper, and they give different outcomes.
Measured on the 19 electrophysiology mice; the paper's mice for this number are not stated.

outcomes.notes: The two-photon calcium imaging (4 C57Bl/6Crl mice, 59 fields of view) is not in the data set, which holds only extracellular recordings; the paper names no deposit of it.
Imaging data not in the data set (see fig4-imaging-intermingled).
Imaging data not in the data set (see fig4-imaging-intermingled).

Contra-preferring neurons are 0.535 of the top quarter of absolute rate differences (228 neurons, binomial p = 0.32) and 0.522 of the top tenth (p = 0.75), a slight majority. Contra-suppression in ipsi-preferring neurons (0.365) is not more frequent than ipsi-suppression in contra-preferring neurons (0.389, Fisher p = 0.49); the whole pre-sample baseline gives 0.367 against 0.391. The four readings of the shared methods give the same (contra fractions 0.522 to 0.558; contra-suppression 0.360 to 0.388 against ipsi-suppression 0.389 to 0.418). The first part holds weakly, the second does not, so the claim holds in part.
deviations: The paper does not define a large difference or contra-suppression; the claims file's readings are used, with the 0.5 s before sample onset as baseline (the data set's compile script's baseline) and the whole pre-sample period as a variant.

outcomes.notes: The photoactivation behaviour of 7 Sim1_KJ18-Cre x Ai32 and 7 Tlx_PL56-Cre x Ai32 mice is not in the data set. In its one Sim1 x Ai32 mouse (ANM218693) all 520 trials with light are of type NaN ("do not analyse"), with eight 1 ms pulses at about 23 mW (session medians), not the 20 Hz trains of 2 ms pulses of Fig. 5.
Photoactivation behaviour not in the data set (see fig5-pt-activation-contralateral-bias).
Photoactivation behaviour not in the data set (see fig5-pt-activation-contralateral-bias).
The high-power photostimulation of trained and untrained mice and of vibrissal motor cortex is not in the data set.
The retrograde tracer anatomy is not in the data set.

The recordings with somatic PT photoactivation during the sample epoch (2 mice, 8 sessions, 91 neurons) are not identified in the data set. Its photostimulation types are axonal tagging (1 and 2), undocumented types 3 to 5 (pulses at 1.8 to 2.8 s) and NaN ("do not analyse"). The NaN-type trials with light, tabulated by mouse and session in the notebook, start in the sample epoch in 367 trials, 347 of them in the two Tlx x Ai32 mice (IT) and the only Sim1 x Ai32 mouse (ANM218693, 3 sessions, 59 units, 135 trials), all as eight 1 ms pulses, at about 23 mW in all but 2 (47 mW), the configuration of the IT test trials. One mouse with 3 sessions cannot be the ED Fig. 7 set, nothing marks a session or trial as an ED Fig. 7 recording, and the description says NaN-type trials are not to be analysed.

findings.statement: The data set holds only the electrophysiology of Figures 2 and 3 and Extended Data Figures 1, 2 and 5. The photoinhibition and photoactivation behaviour (Fig. 1, Fig. 5, ED Figs 3 and 6), the calcium imaging (Fig. 4), the anatomy (ED Fig. 3) and the recordings with somatic PT photoactivation (ED Fig. 7) are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit. Eleven of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

PhotostimulationType takes the values 3, 4 and 5 in 495 trials, all in the two Tlx_PL56-Cre x Ai32 mice ANM218453 and ANM218457 (eight 1 ms pulses at about 23 mW starting 1.8, 2.3 or 2.8 s into the trial), but the data description lists only 0, 1, 2 and NaN. The data set's own compile script treats 1 to 5 as tagging trials.

The NaN-type trials ("photostimulation configurations for testing purposes") carry light in 3,756 trials of all 19 mice, in configurations the description does not give. In three Sim1_KJ18-Cre mice (ANM210861 to ANM210863) they are 50 ms pulses at about 47 mW starting 0.70 to 4.98 s into the trial (session medians 1.9 to 3.2 s). In the other mice without Ai32 they fall mostly outside performing trials, as 50 ms pulses mostly at about 23 mW (session median onset 0.70 s) or 1 ms pulses at about 47 mW (session median onset 0.97 s). In the three Ai32 mice they are eight 1 ms pulses at about 23 mW starting 0.49 to 2.8 s into the trial, 135 of them in the sample epoch of the Sim1 x Ai32 mouse. Which of these, if any, are the ED Fig. 7 PT photostimulation sessions cannot be told.

In session ANM210862_20130627, 43 trials have PhotostimulationType 0 ("non-stimulation trials") but their AOM and laser power traces carry 8 to 22 light pulses of 50 ms at 47.1 mW, starting 1.9 to 4.35 s into the trial (median 3.2 s).

Only neurons that passed the collision test are labelled (45 PT, 27 IT). The 22 pyramidal-tract-activated and 106 intratelencephalic-activated neurons and the 7 untestable ones are not identified, so their counts, latencies and jitter cannot be checked.

The trough-to-peak widths of the deposited mean waveforms put 34 of the 39 unlabelled units below 0.35 ms (158 in all), where the paper and the data description call all 39 intermediate (0.35 to 0.45 ms). The labels split the deposited widths cleanly (FS 0.154 to 0.256 ms, unlabelled 0.307 or 0.410 ms, pyramidal 0.461 to 0.666 ms), so the FS boundary the labels use lies between 0.256 and 0.307 ms, not at the stated 0.35 ms. The cellType labels match the paper's counts; the stated thresholds do not reproduce them from the deposited waveforms.
10 units have spike times out of order (7 in session ANM214429_20130806, and ANM219030_20130829 unit 12, ANM219030_20130831 unit 5, ANM219247_20130920 unit 5).

The lick trace is described only as "licking movement from photodiode"; its baseline (0.07 to 4.83 V per session), scale and sign of excursion differ between sessions, and no detection rule or calibration is given, so the paper's reaction time cannot be recomputed reliably.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the reaction time (61.1 +/- 10.5 ms) found from the photodiode trace, with what threshold, which trials and which mice? On correct trials of the 19 electrophysiology mice, detecting the first departure from the pre-cue baseline by 3, 5 or 10 times the baseline noise gives a mean of per-mouse means of 65 to 104 ms (s.d. across mice 21 to 36 ms), and 5% to 50% of each trial's peak excursion gives 82 to 177 ms.

Question for the paper's authors. How were antidromic spikes told from spontaneous spikes when measuring latency and jitter, and were spikes locked to the pulse over several milliseconds counted? Taking spikes within 1 ms of each neuron's modal latency gives PT 2.7 ms and 0.13 ms and IT 4.6 to 5.0 ms and 0.27 to 0.31 ms, and per-neuron fits of a narrow peak plus background give IT 0.28 to 0.34 ms; only a 0.5 ms window gives the paper's IT jitter of 0.2 ms (0.18 to 0.20 ms).

Question for the paper's authors. Do the PT and IT bootstraps of Fig. 3f, j use all tagged neurons or only the selective ones, and which neurons and window give the P = 0.13 for all task-selective neurons in the late contralateral selectivity? With selective neurons PT is significant (P = 0.033) and IT gives P = 0.74 as printed; with all tagged neurons PT gives P = 0.089. Over the 570 ms before the cue all 912 selective neurons give 9.2% modulation with P = 0.024 (0.022 to 0.024 with lick early trials kept or a 1.5 s response epoch).

The Results give 389 neurons with peri-movement selectivity only and 304 with both, while Fig. 2d shows about 0.43 with both and 0.33 with peri-movement only. The data give 389 with both and 304 peri-movement only, as the figure has.

In 3,707 of 28,465 performing trials the sample or delay epoch differs from 1.3 s by more than 50 ms (up to 14 s), which the data description does not mention. The NWB copies of the sessions omit the photostimulation type, the AOM and laser power traces and GoodTrials, which the analysis needs, so only the MATLAB files support it.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested the helper functions on synthetic inputs and listed the CRCNS bucket itself for the blocked claims. It did not download the data or read the MATLAB scripts the notebook cites. 26 of its 29 outcomes agree with the record as it then stood; it gives not_reproduced for ed1-fast-spiking-properties and contra-ipsi-selectivity-forms and partially_reproduced for antidromic-latency-jitter.

disagreements.reason: FS baseline rates are higher, but FS are more selective under both of the criterion's measures (0.80 vs 0.73 fraction selective; mean absolute difference 2.29 vs 1.53 spikes/s). Only the out-of-criterion normalised variant agrees with the paper.

PT latency and jitter (2.67 ms, 0.11 to 0.13 ms) and PT shorter than IT hold under all readings. IT jitter (0.18 to 0.20) and the tagged mean (0.14) match only with the author's +/-0.5 ms window; with +/-1 ms they are 0.27 to 0.31 and 0.18, out of tolerance. In a synthetic test the +/-0.5 ms window shrinks the s.d. (true 0.3 ms reads as 0.24) and the +/-1 ms window lets in spontaneous spikes, so neither choice is neutral and the match is not robust.

Contra-preferring neurons are a majority of the large group (0.54 and 0.52), but ipsi-preferring neurons show contra-suppression less often than contra-preferring neurons show ipsi-suppression (0.365 vs 0.389). The criterion needs both.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the attempt record, the README and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agrees with every outcome; it withdraws its round-1 not_reproduced for ed1-fast-spiking-properties and contra-ipsi-selectivity-forms. It quotes sentences the printed numbers do not support (cells 8, 10 and 49, the summary, and the record's findings on the type-0 light trials, types 3 to 5, the NaN-type light trials and the ANM218693 trials), and asks for two outputs - the IT jitter without the broad-hump neurons or from a per-neuron fit of a narrow peak plus background, and the fig3fj PT P value with the IT_PT script's filter of more than 15 correct trials of each type. In reply to the points that belong to no single claim, cell 5 now prints the type-0 light trials per trial (47.1 mW, onsets 1.9 to 4.35 s) and types 3 to 5 by mouse, cell 6 the sample-epoch NaN-type configurations and the ANM218693 light trials by type, and the findings and cell 8 are corrected to match; cell 10 now says the 90% range is over the 96.6% of correct trials with a detected onset.
